title: Change a schema, keep the data
description: Add a column to a table that already has rows, and read the rows back afterwards.

files.schema.sql:
-- The schema you want the database to have.
--
-- Ptah reads this file as the desired state, reads the real catalog out of
-- app.db, and works out the difference. You never write ALTER statements here.

CREATE TABLE users (
  id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name  TEXT NOT NULL,
  email TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  title   TEXT NOT NULL,
  done    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id)
);
files.README.md:
# Workspace

    schema.sql   the schema you want
    app.db       the SQLite database you have
    README.md    this file

Ptah's job is the gap between the two.

Try it:

    ptah schema drift --schema-file schema.sql --db-url sqlite://app.db

That reads both and tells you whether they agree. Right now they do.

Add a column to `users` in `schema.sql`:

    active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1

and an index below the tables:

    CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);

Then look before you leap:

    ptah schema apply --schema-file schema.sql --db-url sqlite://app.db --dry-run

Nothing changed — that was a plan. Run it again without `--dry-run` to apply it,
and confirm when asked. Then check the rows are still there in the SQL pane:

    SELECT id, name, active FROM users ORDER BY id;

Everything here runs in this browser tab. Export takes the workspace with you.

baseline.message: This route expects a users table in app.db and a schema.sql in the workspace. One of them is gone, so the steps below no longer describe what you have. Everything still works; Reset puts the scenario back.

steps.title: Explore
steps.caption: Start from existing data
steps.headline: Start by asking whether the file and the database agree.
steps.instruction: app.db already holds three users and four tasks. Ask Ptah whether schema.sql and the database agree.
steps.done: They agree. Exit 0 from schema drift means the desired schema and the live catalog match.

steps.title: Edit schema
steps.caption: Add a column and an index
steps.headline: You describe the schema you want, not the steps to get there.
steps.instruction: Apply the patch, or type the change in yourself: a column in users and an index below the tables. You are describing the schema you want; you never write ALTER here.

action.snippet:
active INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1

CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users (email);
action.hint: The column goes inside the users body, after email. The index goes on its own, below both tables.

steps.done: schema.sql now asks for a column and an index the database does not have.

steps.title: Preview SQL
steps.caption: Review before applying
steps.headline: Review the exact SQL before applying.
steps.instruction: Run apply with --dry-run. It opens app.db to read the catalog, works out the difference and prints the statements. It executes none of them.
steps.done: That plan came out of the real planner. Nothing has been executed: the database still has the columns it started with.

steps.title: Apply
steps.caption: Keep the existing rows
steps.headline: Type YES yourself. Nothing here approves on your behalf.
steps.instruction: Run the same command without --dry-run. Ptah prints the plan again and then waits: type YES at the prompt to proceed. Anything else cancels. Nothing is auto-approved for you.
steps.done: The column and the index are in the catalog, and users still has its three rows.

steps.title: Verify
steps.caption: Query data, check drift
steps.headline: Read the rows back, then ask for drift once more.
steps.instruction: Read the rows back yourself, then ask for drift once more. Both should agree that the change landed and nothing was lost.

action.sql: SELECT id, name, active FROM users ORDER BY id;

steps.done: Desired and actual agree again, checked after the apply rather than before it.

finished.headline: A text file changed and the data survived. That is the whole idea.
finished.caption: Export takes this workspace to the installed CLI, with the commands to continue where you left off.
